text:
Dougie Hamilton is doing most of what New Jersey needs from him and getting little of the credit. He has 12 points in 25 games, right on his usual pace, but only 2 goals on 70 shots. That's 2.9% shooting for a defenseman whose talent range sits between 4 and 7%, and 2 goals against 4.4 expected. The looks are there; the goals tend to follow.

The Devils are good with him on the ice. They control 58% of the expected goals (chance quality) at five on five in his minutes, and he's playing nearly 21 a night. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had him stopping 18% of the entries aimed at him last season (typical is 11%) and in the 94th percentile for chances from in front of the net. Evolving-Hockey noted he faced the other team's best (97th percentile competition), with most of his value coming on the power play.

That's the odd part this season: only 2 of his points have come with the man advantage. At 33 he's still a big-minutes right shot on a team that won seven of its last ten. A few more pucks finding the net would make that obvious again.
headline: Hamilton's shots aren't going in
